moved.sentence: Treat any newer factor revisions as forecasts until officially published, and pin to the current published guidance at https://12factor.net/config.

judged.note: Treating newer factor revisions as forecasts until published, and pinning to the published guidance at 12factor.net/config, is kept at SHOULD with the URL.

moved.sentence: Provide a `.env.example` (committed, no real values) listing every variable the app reads; keep the real `.env` git-ignored and out of images.

judged.note: A committed .env.example with no real values listing every variable, and a git-ignored real .env kept out of images, is kept at SHOULD.

moved.sentence: Validate and coerce config once at boot into a typed config object; the rest of the code reads that object, not `process.env`/`os.environ` directly.

judged.note: Validating and coercing config once at boot into a typed object that the rest of the code reads instead of process.env/os.environ is kept at SHOULD.

moved.sentence: Inject secrets at runtime from a managed secret store (cloud secret manager, orchestrator secret, or vault) rather than baking them into the artifact.

judged.note: Injecting secrets at runtime from a managed secret store rather than baking them into the artifact is kept at SHOULD with all three store examples.

moved.sentence: Treat the choice of a heavyweight secrets platform as adopt-when-measured-need-justifies, not a default (YAGNI) — start with environment injection.

judged.note: A heavyweight secrets platform only on a measured need, not as a default, starting with environment injection, is kept at SHOULD with the YAGNI reason.

moved.sentence: This is engineering guidance and is **NOT** legal advice; consult counsel for regulatory obligations.

judged.note: The not-legal-advice caveat is kept, with consulting counsel for regulatory obligations at SHOULD.

moved.sentence: It is **NOT** internal application constants that stay the same across deploys (routing tables, fixed business rules).

judged.note: That config excludes internal constants that stay the same across deploys, with both examples, is kept in should-keep-constants-in-code, which adds that they SHOULD live in code.
